title: Persistence, checkpoint backup, restore, and replay parity
purpose: Find reachable correctness failures that lose, duplicate, reorder, retain, or restore Ledger state incorrectly across durable persistence, content-addressed checkpoint backup publication, cross-cluster checkpoint restore, and committed-history replay. Apply the companion evidence and ownership contract.
invariants: A prepared-query update that changes target must persist both target and filter before the next checkpoint; historical filter-only updates, deletion, and recreation must survive the latest checkpoint without resurrecting an old definition.

Post-checkpoint audited projections and durable admission dependencies must retain parity, including balances and volumes, transactions and references, ledger info/account types/default enforcement, the monotonic ledger-ID allocator, boundaries and mirror progress, signing keys/config and cascaded revocation, cluster policy, maintenance mode, sink configuration, query-checkpoint state/counters/schedule, index registry, numscripts, reversion state, and frozen idempotency outcomes where present at this SHA. The audit must inventory current producers rather than treating this list as exhaustive or promising retention beyond documented lifecycle rules.

Restore preparation must preserve the captured applied-index genesis boundary while removing or marking source-cluster-local state according to contract: persisted node/cluster identity, peers, transient backup jobs, cache and bloom state, and query-checkpoint provenance must not leak stale authority into the restored cluster. Restored business records may retain source provenance, but destination progress certificates must bind to the restored cluster's captured boundary.

An acknowledged committed write must survive the persistence boundary promised by the production path, and replay of the same committed history must reconstruct the same externally observable ledger state. Sequence numbers, offsets, watermarks, manifests, and checkpoints must not advance ahead of the durable rows they certify.

Restore parity evidence must use an oracle independent of the restore writer where practical and must include CheckStore on the restored primary store without findings or errors. Checker success is corroboration, not a substitute for direct logical comparisons; a checker defect belongs to integrity-verifier-soundness unless a restore path corrupted the input.

Caches, preload state, peer read stores, usage stores, and other rebuildable local projections must not become authoritative over restored primary state. Their discard or reconstruction must converge from the complete restored history without overwriting primary values captured in the latest checkpoint.

Raft-applied drain marker and release state advance with the applied index in the same Pebble batch, and qualifying member status fsyncs the WAL before certifying that index. Restart and in-cluster snapshot sync restore an active cutoff before admission; cross-cluster restore deliberately discards the cluster-transient drain state.

Follower-sync staging holds exactly one session's checkpoint when activated. Every session retry against the same donor, like every donor fallback, empties the staging directory and resets progress before the new session. A file left by an earlier session that the new manifest does not list must never reach Pebble open: tied marker.manifest iterations resolve by unsorted directory order and can open a stale MANIFEST over the new WAL.

Every committed effect before a backup capture point that must survive cross-cluster restore is present in the flushed Pebble checkpoint, including audit history, primary projections, and operational policy. A second checkpoint after a committed mutation restores that mutation without an exported delta.

A metadata-only Numscript execution is an audited business effect even when it creates no transaction. A checkpoint taken after that execution must capture the updated account metadata and audit history without inventing a transaction, reference, or next-ID advance. Restore must preserve those values and the next admitted operation.

The backup uploads and verifies every checkpoint file, including a Pebble WAL file if present; publishes the new manifest only after all required objects exist; and prunes objects only after publication. A failed upload or manifest write leaves the previous manifest restorable.

Restore rejects legacy manifests containing exports or a separate cluster-policy override before activating staging. Offline bootstrap and gRPC restore use the same checkpoint-only contract. This is the maintainer-approved PR #2600 RC artifact exception; rejection is not evidence that the old artifact remains recoverable after source loss.
adversarial_questions: Can a successful audited order write no ledger log, share old logs through idempotency, or emit multiple logs, and does the next checkpoint include the resulting durable state and audit evidence coherently?

Can source-cluster applied indexes in restored query-checkpoint or business rows be mistaken for destination progress, especially when the new Raft domain numerically overtakes them? Are restored markers, genesis boundary, publication and later deletion handled atomically enough to avoid an intermediate certificate?

Does a newly added durable cluster-local key inherit the whole-zone delete, or can it leak source identity or authority into the destination? Does a captured failed or successful business proposal leave the destination HLC behind the restored audit head?

Is a candidate actually a restore/replay root cause, or only generic process re-exec, Raft snapshot transport/install ordering, checker blindness, read-index lag/rebuild, retry identity, configuration admission, or filesystem confinement already owned by a neighboring manifest?

Can a follower-sync session retry, donor fallback, or abandoned attempt leave files the next manifest does not list (MANIFEST, WAL, marker, OPTIONS, SST) in the staging directory that is activated and opened? Which checkpoint does Pebble open when two sessions' marker files tie, and does the restored applied index then cover entries whose effects are absent?
Can a confirmed transaction or policy update before the capture point be omitted by the memtable flush or checkpoint file enumeration?
Can object reuse, upload failure, manifest failure, or prune failure make the published manifest point to missing or corrupt content?
Can either restore entry point accept a legacy export manifest or activate a partial second checkpoint?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: Exercise DeleteLedger after the checkpoint against a ledger with balances, metadata, transactions/references, indexes and registry rows, numscripts, reversions, mirror/boundary state and other current ledger-scoped projections. Compare complete logical keysets with uninterrupted execution and verify no checkpoint-era child survives; include a matched live ledger to detect over-broad range deletion.

Exercise post-checkpoint signing registration and cascaded revocation, policy and maintenance transitions, prepared-query target/filter updates followed by deletion or recreation, query-checkpoint create/delete/counter progress and schedule set/delete/recreate ordering, index create/drop/retype, ledger promote, account-type changes, idempotent success/failure reuse and reversion. Assert values and future gate decisions rather than row counts alone.

Run applicable existing focused suites, such as go test ./internal/infra/backup/... and the repository-managed restore E2E/model targets only when their documented infrastructure is available. Race or Antithesis runs provide evidence only for reached assertions; use deterministic barriers and never time.Sleep. If a new reproducer would require tracked edits, leave a precise plan for a separately authorized engineering task.

Fail a first follower-sync session after it staged a Pebble file set, retry against the same donor with a different manifest (as after a donor restart that flushed its WAL), and assert the staging directory holds exactly the second manifest's files and progress counters match it.

Create a checkpoint, commit a distinct transaction and policy mutation, create a second checkpoint, restore it through gRPC and offline bootstrap, and compare exact values plus CheckStore results. No third checkpoint may mask the second.

Run TestBackup_NumscriptRestoreParity with a metadata-only script after the first checkpoint; take a second checkpoint and restore it. Assert exact source/restored account metadata and transaction sets, clean CheckStore, and a subsequent admitted scripted operation.
Inject upload, manifest-write, and prune failures and verify the previously published manifest remains restorable and retries clean harmless orphans.
Mutate a manifest with exports or a clusterPolicy override and require both restore entry points to reject it before activation.
